message.content:
You are auditing Android/Kotlin AI-agent "skill" files for the "Image loading (Coil)" topic across up to three source repos that are being merged into ONE Claude Code plugin. When multiple skills auto-trigger on the same code, contradictory guidance is a real defect.

Read the FULL content of every SKILL.md in these directories, plus any references/*.md files inside them (use Glob or Bash 'ls -R' first to discover reference files):

- [ahmed] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/everything-claude-code-mobile/skills/image-loading/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [rcosteira] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/android-skills/plugins/android-skills/skills/coil-compose/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)

Produce:
1. contradictions — cases where two sources give ACTUALLY OPPOSING advice on the SAME specific technical point (not merely different depth or wording of the same principle). Name both sources (labels: "ahmed" / "chris" / "rcosteira"), state each claim, and cite evidence (file path + the specific lines/quote).
2. bugs — code that is broken, will not compile, or is technically WRONG (e.g. catches and swallows CancellationException, loses state across config change, references undefined symbols, wrong plugin/order). severity: critical | major | minor. Cite the file + evidence.
3. depthComparison — which source is most detailed/actionable here and why.
4. uniqueValue — what each source covers that the OTHERS DO NOT (worth keeping regardless of who dominates).

Be precise; cite real file content. Do NOT invent contradictions where sources only differ in depth — that is the most common false positive. Set cluster="image-loading".

Trigger keywords — silent fallback, default value, swallowed exception, empty catch, error handling, defensive coding, guard clause. Do NOT use this skill for designing immutable data models (use immutability) or for forward-compatible unused parameters (use forward-compat-slots).
- core:forward-compat-slots: Apply the forward-compatible reserved-injection-slot convention — a constructor or function parameter prefixed with underscore AND typed optional is an intentionally-unused dependency slot kept so future callers can inject it without touching every call site. - core:immutability: Minimize mutability — default domain types to immutable, derive new state with copy-on-write instead of mutating in place, never mutate function arguments, and keep a pure functional core with side effects pushed to a thin imperative shell. Trigger keywords — mutable state, in-place mutation, copy-on-write, immutable, frozen, readonly, value object, functional core, shared state bug. Covers low coupling and high cohesion; the common module types (app/feature/data/core); the rule that feature modules never depend on other feature modules (the app module mediates, usually via the navigation graph); keeping each module's public surface minimal with Kotlin internal; preferring Gradle implementation over api to avoid leaking transitive deps; and passing primitive IDs (not whole objects) across boundaries. Do NOT use for KMP commonMain source-set layout (a different axis — use kmp-multiplatform/kmp-structure); for in-app layering use android-architecture, UI state android-ui-layer, repositories android-data-layer, Compose jetpack-compose, plain Kotlin style kotlin-style.

Do NOT use for KMP commonMain shared code (use kmp-multiplatform); for the overview use android-architecture, repositories android-data-layer, Compose recomposition/side-effects jetpack-compose, Compose-MP UI kmp-compose-mp-ui, plain Kotlin style kotlin-style.
- kotlin:jetpack-compose: Native-Android Jetpack Compose UI discipline — load when reading/writing/reviewing @Composable code in a native-Android app/feature module (androidx.compose.* imports). Covers state hoisting (stateless composable, value down / events up); recomposition and stability (@Stable/@Immutable, stable params that let Compose skip, unstable collections, stable lambdas); the side-effect APIs (LaunchedEffect and its key restart, rememberCoroutineScope, DisposableEffect/onDispose, rememberUpdatedState, derivedStateOf, snapshotFlow, produceState); remember vs remember(key) vs rememberSaveable; stable keys for lazy-list items; modifier order and the modifier-parameter convention; slot APIs; previews/testing. Do NOT use for Compose Multiplatform / non-Android targets (Skia canvas, UIKitView, iOS/desktop/web — use kmp-compose-mp-ui) or KMP commonMain shared code (kmp-multiplatform); for the architecture overview use android-architecture, ViewModel/UI-state rules android-ui-layer, plain Kotlin style kotlin-style.
- kotlin:kmp-compose-mp-ui: Depth guidance for Compose Multiplatform UI across non-Android targets (iOS, desktop, web/Wasm). Covers the central fact that Compose MP renders via a Skiko/Skia canvas, not native UIKit/SwiftUI widgets, and what follows (identical look by default, native-view interop, simulated-native iOS scroll physics since 1.8.0, on-device verification of canvas/interop/accessibility); choosing Compose MP vs native UI per target; stability (iOS Stable since 1.8.0, desktop Stable, Web/Wasm Beta); resources, fonts, density; navigation. Trigger keywords — Compose Multiplatform, Skiko, desktop Compose, Compose for Web, Wasm, UIKitView, compose-resources, navigation. Do NOT use for Android-only Jetpack Compose, non-UI logic (use kmp-structure), or Swift/Kotlin interop (use kmp-interop).
- kotlin:kmp-interop: Depth guidance for Kotlin <-> Swift/Objective-C interop and per-platform networking in KMP. Covers refining the ObjC header Kotlin exports to Swift (@HiddenFromObjC, @ObjCName, @ShouldRefineInSwift), why not to expose Flow directly to Swift (use SKIE) and that suspend->Swift async is officially experimental, exported-surface quirks (top-level funcs become <FileName>Kt classes, generics only on classes, no default args), and Ktor with ktor-client-core in commonMain plus an engine per platform (Darwin/OkHttp/CIO). Use when designing the API a Swift/iOS app consumes from shared Kotlin, debugging an awkward generated Swift signature, deciding how to bridge Flow or suspend to Swift, or wiring the Ktor client. Trigger keywords — Swift interop, Objective-C, @ObjCName, @ShouldRefineInSwift, SKIE, Flow to Swift, suspend async, Ktor, Darwin, OkHttp. Do NOT use for shared logic structure (use kmp-structure), Compose UI (use kmp-compose-mp-ui), or everyday Kotlin language style (use kotlin-style).
- kotlin:kmp-multiplatform: Kotlin Multiplatform framework rules for shared code — load when reading, writing, or reviewing files under a commonMain or commonTest source set (auto-scoped to **/commonMain/**/*.kt and **/commonTest/**/*.kt), or on demand for KMP layout questions. Covers where shared code lives and the one-way platform->common dependency, what to share vs keep native, the commonMain-only coroutine constraint (Dispatchers.Default not IO, because IO is JVM/Native-only and breaks JS/Wasm), the expect/actual escalation ladder, and commonTest using kotlin.test only (no JUnit, which breaks Native). Keywords — KMP, multiplatform, commonMain, commonTest, expect, actual, source set, Dispatchers in common code, JS, Wasm. Do NOT use for native-Android-only code (there Dispatchers.IO is correct — use the android skills), everyday Kotlin language style (kotlin-style), source-set depth (kmp-structure), Compose-MP UI (kmp-compose-mp-ui), or Swift interop (kmp-interop).

196	@Observable
197	class ImageCache {
198	    static let shared = ImageCache()
199	
200	    private let cache = NSCache<NSString, UIImage>()
201	    private let session = URLSession.shared
202	
203	    init() {
204	        cache.countLimit = 100
205	        cache.totalCostLimit = 50 * 1024 * 1024 // 50 MB
206	    }
207	
208	    func image(for url: URL) async throws -> UIImage {
209	        let key = url.absoluteString as NSString
210	
211	        if let cached = cache.object(forKey: key) {
212	            return cached
213	        }
214	
215	        let (data, _) = try await session.data(from: url)
216	        guard let image = UIImage(data: data) else {
217	            throw ImageError.decodingFailed
218	        }
219	
220	        cache.setObject(image, forKey: key, cost: data.count)
221	        return image
222	    }
223

348	// iOS: Downsample large images
349	func downsample(imageAt url: URL, to pointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat) -> UIImage? {
350	    let imageSourceOptions = [kCGImageSourceShouldCache: false] as CFDictionary
351	    guard let imageSource = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url as CFURL, imageSourceOptions) else {
352	        return nil
353	    }
354	
355	    let maxDimension = max(pointSize.width, pointSize.height) * scale
356	    let options: [CFString: Any] = [
357	        kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true,
358	        kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true,
359	        kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true,
360	        kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: maxDimension
361	    ]
362	
363	    guard let cgImage = CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex(imageSource, 0, options as CFDictionary) else {
364	        return nil
365	    }
366	    return UIImage(cgImage: cgImage)
367	}

405	## Best Practices
406	
407	- Always provide placeholder and error drawables for every image load.
408	- Use `crossfade(true)` for smoother transitions from placeholder to loaded image.
409	- Configure disk cache size based on app needs (50-200 MB typical).
410	- Set memory cache to 20-25% of available app memory.
411	- Downsample images to the display size; never load a 4000px image into a 200dp view.
412	- Use `ContentScale.Crop` for fixed-size containers, `ContentScale.Fit` for flexible ones.
413	- Preload images for items about to scroll into view in lists.
414	- Clear caches on low-memory warnings (`onTrimMemory` / `didReceiveMemoryWarning`).
415	- For lists, set explicit sizes on image composables to prevent layout jumps during load.
416	- Use shimmer effects instead of spinner placeholders for a more polished loading experience.

6	# Coil 3 for Compose & Compose Multiplatform
7	
8	This reference covers the KMP specifics and two performance guardrails, not the basics of `AsyncImage` / `SubcomposeAsyncImage` / `ImageRequest` / `placeholder` / `error` / `contentDescription` / a shared `ImageLoader`.
9	
10	## KMP: `LocalPlatformContext`, not `LocalContext`
11	
12	Coil 3 is fully multiplatform — `AsyncImage` / `SubcomposeAsyncImage` / `rememberAsyncImagePainter` are identical in `commonMain`, with **no `expect`/`actual` needed**. The one swap: use `LocalPlatformContext.current`, not `LocalContext.current` (Android-only; a compile error in `commonMain`). It resolves to `android.content.Context` on Android and `PlatformContext.INSTANCE` on other targets.
13	
14	```kotlin
15	// commonMain — works on all platforms
16	AsyncImage(
17	    model = ImageRequest.Builder(LocalPlatformContext.current).data(url).crossfade(true).build(),
18	    contentDescription = "User avatar",
19	    modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp).clip(CircleShape),
20	)
21	```
22	
23	**Singleton setup (KMP):** call `SingletonImageLoader.setSafe { ImageLoader.Builder(it).crossfade(true).build() }` once early in the app lifecycle, or pass an `imageLoader` explicitly. **`coil-compose` vs `coil-compose-core`:** with `coil-compose`, `AsyncImage` *without* an `imageLoader` argument uses the singleton automatically; with `coil-compose-core`, the `imageLoader` parameter is **required** (no singleton convenience). Add a platform network engine as needed (e.g. `coil-network-ktor3` for KMP).
24	
25	## Two performance guardrails
26	
27	**`SubcomposeAsyncImage` is significantly slower than regular composition — never use it inside `LazyColumn` / `LazyRow`.** It creates a subcomposition per item; during scroll that overhead accumulates into visible jank. For custom loading/error states in a list, use `AsyncImage` with `placeholder` / `error` parameters instead — same visual result, no subcomposition.
28	
29	**`rememberAsyncImagePainter` does NOT infer the display size from layout constraints** — without an explicit `.size()` it loads the image at its original dimensions (a 4000×3000 photo shown at 64dp still occupies the full bitmap in memory → OOM in a 50-item list). Reach for it only when a `Painter` is strictly required (`Canvas`, `Icon`, a custom draw); always pass `.size()`. Otherwise use `AsyncImage`, which sizes automatically.
30	
31	```kotlin
32	// only when a Painter is genuinely required — explicit size is mandatory
33	val painter = rememberAsyncImagePainter(
34	    ImageRequest.Builder(LocalPlatformContext.current).data(url).size(Size(128, 128)).build(),
35	)
36	Image(painter = painter, contentDescription = null)
37	```

contradictions.topic: Which context to pass into ImageRequest.Builder in Compose with Coil 3 (LocalContext vs LocalPlatformContext)
contradictions.claimA: Build ImageRequest with LocalContext.current; used consistently throughout the skill.
contradictions.claimB: Do NOT use LocalContext.current; use LocalPlatformContext.current. LocalContext is Android-only and is a compile error in commonMain, whereas LocalPlatformContext resolves to android.content.Context on Android and works on all targets.
contradictions.evidence: Both target Coil 3 (ahmed declares io.coil-kt.coil3 3.0.4). ahmed SKILL.md uses ImageRequest.Builder(LocalContext.current) at lines 70, 87, 337, 377. rcosteira SKILL.md lines 10-12: 'use LocalPlatformContext.current, not LocalContext.current (Android-only; a compile error in commonMain)' and line 17 shows ImageRequest.Builder(LocalPlatformContext.current). Direct opposing recommendation on the same API call; in a merged plugin both auto-trigger on Coil-3 Compose code and ahmed's guidance breaks any KMP/commonMain usage. (Scope nuance: ahmed is Android-only where LocalContext still compiles, but rcosteira's blanket 'not LocalContext' directly conflicts.)

contradictions.topic: How to render custom image loading/error states: SubcomposeAsyncImage vs AsyncImage placeholder/error
contradictions.claimA: Use SubcomposeAsyncImage for custom loading/error states (documents a User-avatar example with a ShimmerBox loading state and an error Icon) with no performance caveat, and recommends shimmer effects for loading.
contradictions.claimB: SubcomposeAsyncImage is significantly slower than regular composition and must NEVER be used inside LazyColumn/LazyRow; for custom loading/error states in a list use AsyncImage with placeholder/error parameters instead — same visual result, no subcomposition.
contradictions.evidence: ahmed SKILL.md lines 37-64 (SubcomposeAsyncImage avatar with when(painter.state){Loading->ShimmerBox; Error->Icon...}) plus best-practice line 416 ('Use shimmer effects instead of spinner placeholders'). rcosteira SKILL.md line 27: 'SubcomposeAsyncImage is significantly slower... never use it inside LazyColumn / LazyRow... use AsyncImage with placeholder / error parameters instead.' ahmed promotes exactly the approach (SubcomposeAsyncImage + shimmer for avatars, a classic list item) that rcosteira prohibits for that use case.

bugs.description: DiskCache.Builder().directory(...) is passed a java.io.File, but Coil 3's DiskCache.Builder.directory() takes an okio.Path (no File overload). With the declared io.coil-kt.coil3:3.0.4 dependency this is a type-mismatch compile error. Occurs twice.
bugs.evidence: Lines 116 and 137: .directory(context.cacheDir.resolve("image_cache")) and .directory(androidContext().cacheDir.resolve("image_cache")). context.cacheDir.resolve(...) returns java.io.File; Coil 3 requires okio.Path (e.g. via .toOkioPath()). Note the file DID adopt other Coil 3 APIs (MemoryCache.Builder() no-arg + maxSizePercent(context,0.25) at lines 107-110), so the File-based directory call is an unconverted Coil 2 signature.

bugs.description: BlurTransformation(LocalContext.current, radius = 25f) references a Coil 2 API. Coil 3 removed the context-based BlurTransformation; it is an undefined symbol under the declared coil3 3.0.4 dependency, so following this suggested option fails to compile.
bugs.evidence: Line 93: '// or BlurTransformation(LocalContext.current, radius = 25f)' offered as a transformations() option. CircleCropTransformation() and RoundedCornersTransformation(16f) on the surrounding lines do exist in Coil 3; BlurTransformation with a Context parameter does not.

bugs.description: ImageLoader.Builder(context).respectCacheHeaders(true) is a Coil 2 ImageLoader.Builder method. In Coil 3 respectCacheHeaders was removed from ImageLoader.Builder (HTTP cache-header behavior moved to the network layer / CacheStrategy), so this likely will not compile against coil3 3.0.4. (Plausible / version-dependent.)
bugs.evidence: Line 119: .respectCacheHeaders(true) chained on ImageLoader.Builder(context) in the Custom ImageLoader Configuration block (lines 105-120).

bugs.description: Out-of-scope (iOS/Swift, not Coil/Android) but matches a flagged anti-pattern: the CachedAsyncImage .task swallows every error, including task-cancellation, with only a '// log error' comment, then unconditionally sets isLoading=false. A cancelled load is silently treated as a normal completion.
bugs.evidence: Lines 256-262: do { image = try await ImageCache.shared.image(for: url) } catch { // log error } isLoading = false. URLSession/task cancellation throws are caught and discarded here.

input.depthComparison: By volume and copy-paste breadth, ahmed is far more detailed (416 lines vs 37): it covers AsyncImage, SubcomposeAsyncImage, the ImageRequest builder, transformations, a full custom ImageLoader (memory + disk cache), Koin DI wiring, preloading, downsampling with Precision, reusable Avatar/CardImage/ShimmerBox/ImageErrorState composables, and an explicit best-practices checklist (plus a complete iOS/SwiftUI parallel). For a pure-Android app it is the more actionable, ready-to-paste reference. However it targets Coil 3 yet still ships several Coil-2-era API signatures (DiskCache directory File, BlurTransformation, respectCacheHeaders), so some of its depth is subtly wrong for the version it declares. rcosteira is deliberately terse and explicitly scopes OUT the basics, but is more technically precise and correct for Coil 3: it nails the KMP context swap (LocalPlatformContext), the coil-compose vs coil-compose-core singleton distinction, SingletonImageLoader.setSafe, and two performance guardrails with rationale (no SubcomposeAsyncImage in lazy lists; rememberAsyncImagePainter needs explicit .size() or OOM) — the 'why/when' that ahmed omits. Net: ahmed is deepest for pure-Android usage breadth; rcosteira is the most correct and highest-signal on Coil 3 semantics, KMP, and performance. They are largely complementary rather than redundant.

uniqueValue.whatIsUnique: Custom ImageLoader configuration (memory + disk cache sizing, respectCacheHeaders); Koin DI integration via setSingletonImageLoaderFactory; image preloading via context.imageLoader.enqueue; transformations examples (CircleCrop / RoundedCorners / Blur); reusable Avatar, CardImage, ShimmerBox, and ImageErrorState-with-retry composables; explicit downsampling with .size()+Precision.INEXACT; an explicit best-practices checklist (cache sizes, ContentScale.Crop vs Fit, onTrimMemory, explicit list sizes); and a full iOS/SwiftUI + cross-platform section (phase-based AsyncImage, NSCache-based ImageCache, CachedAsyncImage, CGImageSource downsampling).

KMP/Compose Multiplatform setup: LocalPlatformContext.current and the fact that AsyncImage/SubcomposeAsyncImage/rememberAsyncImagePainter need no expect/actual; the coil-compose vs coil-compose-core distinction (singleton auto-use vs required imageLoader arg); SingletonImageLoader.setSafe and coil-network-ktor3 for KMP; the performance guardrail that SubcomposeAsyncImage must never be used in LazyColumn/LazyRow (subcomposition-per-item jank); and the rememberAsyncImagePainter pitfall that it does NOT infer size from layout constraints so an explicit .size() is mandatory to avoid loading full-resolution bitmaps (OOM). None of these are covered by ahmed.
